lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Stonebridge should appear before Crescent.
items.because: Stonebridge is the more recent role.

items.says: Order bullets within each role by relevance and impact.
Use a consistent date format and separator throughout.
Use en dashes consistently in date ranges.
Ensure the profile URL is the actual customized LinkedIn URL and is clickable.
Consider adding city and state for location-dependent or hybrid applications.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for U.S. applications.
items.because: They are not normally included and can expose you to age- or nationality-related bias.

items.says: Use standard city/state format if Metro City is not fictionalized.
Buying more same-duration fixed-rate bonds does not hedge the bank’s interest-rate exposure.
items.because: It generally increases duration and interest-rate exposure.

items.says: Identify the actual exposure, instrument, and direction of the hedge.
items.because: The transaction described does not have the claimed mechanics.

items.says: Clarify your degree of ownership of the hedge.
items.because: A credit analyst independently hedging a bank’s securities portfolio may sound implausible.

items.says: Add the number of applications reviewed if substantial and nonconfidential.
items.because: It would show scale.

items.says: Define “early defaults” by time period or delinquency standard.
items.because: It would make the risk outcome credible.

items.says: Establish that the no-increase claim was measured over a sufficient post-change period.
Avoid implying sole causation for the threshold changes if a broader team approved or implemented them.
Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The role ended in 2022.

items.says: Clarify whether you created, redesigned, or maintained the checklist.
items.because: The scope of ownership is ambiguous.

items.says: Identify the measurement periods behind the reduction from seven missed tests to one.
Consider adding portfolio size or borrower count.
items.because: It would show scale.

items.says: Clarify whether six to three hours is an average or median rather than true of each memo.
items.because: “Each” can sound overly absolute.

items.says: Add the template’s adoption or volume if available.
Specify what “USD 600M” measures.
items.because: It could refer to revenue, assets, or another scale indicator.

items.says: Define the forecast-error metric and the period it stayed below 4%.
Soften the claim that the forecast enabled the early debt paydown if other factors drove it.
items.because: The direct causal link needs confirmation.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30 items include intercompany eliminations or are all reconciliations.
Add the technology used if it is marketable and you built the automation.
Indicate whether the five-day close was sustained for multiple cycles.
items.because: It would make the result more credible.

items.says: Add the total capital value reviewed if available.
Add an outcome beyond standardization.
items.because: Faster review, fewer revisions, or more consistent approvals would show impact.

items.says: Avoid saying “every request” unless adoption was complete.
items.because: The wording implies absolute adoption.

items.says: Clarify whether you built the template, modeled the projects, or governed the assumptions.
items.because: Those indicate different levels of responsibility.

items.says: Open with a consistent past-tense action structure.
Remove the comma before “cut.”
items.because: It separates the long subject phrase from the verb and makes the sentence awkward.

items.says: Simplify the sentence.
items.because: It contains three major activities plus a result.

items.says: Clarify what was tested against the prior closes.
Clarify whether the reduction to 90 entries occurred after implementation.
FCFE should not be discounted at WACC.
items.because: FCFE is discounted at the cost of equity, while FCFF is discounted at WACC.

items.says: Verify which cash-flow measure and discount rate you actually used.
Add transaction scale, a valuation range, sensitivity work, a recommendation, or the deal outcome if nonconfidential.
items.because: The bullet describes a standard task without demonstrating impact.

items.says: Add an outcome of training the controllers.
items.because: Adoption, fewer errors, or fewer support requests would show impact.

items.says: Clarify whether this budgeting template is related to the earlier capital-plan template.
items.because: If so, the material may appear repetitive.

items.says: Use the current date range only if the project is still actively maintained or expanded.
Reconsider listing Excel in the project heading.
items.because: Excel is already the only tool listed in Skills.

items.says: Identify the project more precisely as self-directed investment or valuation work if useful.
Reconsider treating proximity to market price as the main proof of model quality.
items.because: It can suggest assumptions were calibrated to the market rather than developed independently.

items.says: Add the valuation date and emphasize independent assumptions, the investment conclusion, or key drivers.
Clarify whether comparable-company analysis was a cross-check or an independently weighted method.
A fall from USD 50 to USD 40 is 20%, not 25%.
Call the rate movement a percentage-point increase rather than a “point” increase.
items.because: “Point” is ambiguous.

items.says: Clarify whether USD 50 and USD 40 are model outputs rather than market prices.
Consider identifying the starting discount rate.
items.because: Sensitivity depends heavily on the base assumption.

items.says: Clarify how accuracy was measured for a current 10-year forecast.
items.because: Future periods cannot yet be evaluated.

items.says: If the result came from historical backtesting, identify it and define the accuracy metric.
Calling the change from 70% to 82% a 12% increase is statistically incorrect as written.
items.because: It is 12 percentage points, or approximately 17.1% relative.

items.says: Explain what was forecast and how rate-case timing improved the measurement.
Ensure the backtest did not use future information.
items.because: That would make the result unreliable.

items.says: Consider placing the student fund under activities, leadership, or additional experience rather than projects.
items.because: The best section depends on how the fund operated.

items.says: Add the fund’s assets under management or strategy if available.
items.because: It would establish scale.

items.says: Remove or substantially change the FP&A support bullet unless the fund had an FP&A team.
items.because: It sounds inconsistent with an investment-fund role.

items.says: Specify the actual analysis or reporting responsibility.
items.because: The broad support statement is generic and provides no scale or outcome.

items.says: Add fund size, reporting frequency, performance period, or benchmark if available.
Clarify whether you calculated returns, automated the report, selected the benchmark, or only redesigned its presentation.
Add the number of analysts supported or a measurable onboarding benefit.
items.because: Without demonstrable impact, this bullet is weaker than the others.

items.says: Specify the substantive model areas documented.
Add other tools you can credibly use.
items.because: Listing only Excel may make your technical range appear narrow given the automation, reconciliations, templates, and account mapping described.

items.says: Align the methods list more closely with capabilities demonstrated in the bullets.
items.because: Capital budgeting, financial-statement spreading, covenant monitoring, variance analysis, and close-process improvement are relevant examples.
